title: Understanding Image Quality for Better Conversion Choices
description: Learn how image resolution, compression, and format selection affect the quality of converted images.
author: Converigo
og_image_alt: Visual explanation of image quality factors

sections.title: Resolution and detail
sections.content: Higher resolution usually preserves more detail, but it also increases file size. Balancing detail and size is a common part of image conversion work.

sections.title: Compression effects
sections.content: Compression can make file sizes smaller, but it may also reduce visible quality. The best setting depends on how the image will be used.

sections.title: Match the format to the purpose
sections.content: Photography and web graphics often need different approaches. Choosing the right format and quality setting is important for both appearance and performance.

faq.question: What is the difference between resolution and quality?
faq.answer: Resolution affects the amount of detail captured, while quality depends on how that detail is preserved during compression and conversion.

faq.question: Should I always choose the highest quality setting?
faq.answer: Not always. High quality is useful for archival or print workflows, but it may create large files for web sharing.

faq.question: How can I tell if a conversion reduced quality too much?
faq.answer: Compare the output on screen for blur, artifacts, or visible blockiness, especially in sharp edges and small text.
